title: Disappearing Species

card.teaser: A koala silhouette filled with cooling towers. One image instead of a page of statistics.

summary: An environmental awareness poster using a black koala silhouette and cooling towers cut out of its body to connect endangered wildlife with industrial pollution and habitat loss.

hero.alt: A poster of a koala silhouette containing cooling towers and smoke.

text: Inspired by a World Wildlife Fund brief, this project explores how an environmental issue can be communicated through a single image rather than a large amount of explanatory text.
I focused on the relationship between endangered wildlife and industrial activity, looking for a way to make that connection visible within the animal itself.

rows.heading: Words before pictures
rows.body: I wrote two wordlists, one for the koala and one for what threatens it: fire, oil, logging, power lines, roads, city blocks. Then I turned the words into small icons to see which ones were strong enough to share a shape with the animal.
rows.caption: Research.

rows.heading: Cutting into the koala
rows.body: I drew koala silhouettes in different poses and tried cutting different shapes out of their bodies. The cooling tower, with its plume of steam, was the one that read at a glance, so it stayed.
rows.caption: Sketches.

deliverables: Research into endangered species and environmental issues
finalDesign: The first icon sheets had a long list of threats: fire, oil, logging, roads, power lines. The cooling tower won because its plume of steam reads at a glance and fits inside a koala's body. The other cut-outs needed explaining. I also left out numbers, since the brief was one image, and the koala and the factory share a shape, so no caption has to connect them.
pull: If the image needs a caption to connect the two, it isn't done.
